 Heat center Bam Adebayo on the cover art of NBA 2K27 Vice City Edition. (FP NetSuite courtesy) 
 By Ira Winderman | iwinderman@sunsentinel.com | South Florida Sun Sentinel PUBLISHED: November 16, 2026 at 2:35 PM EST | UPDATED: November 16, 2026 at 4:55 PM EST Getting your Trinity Audio player ready... MIAMI — Worlds have officially collided for the Miami Heat ahead of the “A Night in Vice City” takeover on Wednesday night at Kaseya Center for the team’s game against the Milwaukee Bucks.
 Monday, the NBA 2K27 video game announced a partnership with Rockstar Games’ Grand Theft Auto series that will have Heat center Bam Adebayo on the cover of a NBA 2K27 Vice City edition.
 The NBA 2K27 Vice City edition featuring the three-time NBA All-Star on the cover of the limited-time collaboration will be available by download Nov. 27 through Jan. 15.
 That edition of 2K features an extensive update with Vice City-themed content and rewards across The City and MyTeam playing options.
 “It’s hard to describe what it feels like to see yourself on the cover of a game you grew up playing,” Adebayo said in coordination with Monday’s announcement. “I’ve also spent my whole career in Miami, so being on the NBA 2K27 Vice City Edition cover is special to me and to this city.
 “The culture of Miami is special and getting to see everyone experience that through the game is what’s so exciting.”
 In addition, it was announced that GTA+ Members on PS5 and XBOX Series X|S can play NBA 2K27 at no extra cost through January 15.
 For Wednesday night’s game against the Bucks , NBA 2K will take over the 601 event space at Kaseya Center with a 2K Mart-meets-Vice City  immersive activation , featuring limited-edition merchandise giveaways, and photo opportunities.
 During the game against the Bucks, the Heat will wear special-edition Nike x Cactus Jack uniforms, uniforms that now also will be featured in NBA 2K27.
 Doors for the 7 p.m. tip for the nationally televised game (ESPN nationally; Local 10 and other South Florida affiliates locally) will open early, at 5 p.m., to accommodate those seeking to purchase the limited-edition Heat “Vice City” jerseys, with a limit of one per customer.
 Another ring
 Heat forward Giannis Antetokounmpo soon will be adding another championship ring to his collection.
 Already with a bauble from the Milwaukee Bucks’ 2021 NBA title, it was confirmed that his ownership stake in the Milwaukee Brewers means another ring is on the way.
 “Everybody who’s an owner would be getting a ring,” Brewers president of business operations Rick Schlesinger said, according to Milwaukee’s Journal Sentinel . “Sure. He’s an owner.”
 Antetokounmpo became a minority owner of the Brewers in 2021.
 During the Brewers’ run to their championship, Antetokounmpo said, “It’s incredible. I’m so happy for the team. It’s been a lot of years in the works.”

 The Brewers are in the process of designing the ring.
 “There is a relatively short window of time to get the rings designed because production of the rings is something that is done by hand and it takes a long time,” Schlesinger said. “You want to make sure the rings are available for our players and our front office staff when the season starts in 2027.”
 Or, in Antetokounmpo’s case, before the end of the Heat’s season.
 The Heat’s lone scheduled visit to Milwaukee is Feb. 24.
 For Antetokounmpo, the share of the Brewers is part of a diversified sports portfolio, also with ownership stakes in Nashville SC of Major League Soccer, Los Angeles Golf Club of The Golf League and the Milwaukee Wave indoor soccer team.
 Player of Week
 For the 29th time in his career, Antetokounmpo was named NBA Player of the Week.
 Monday’s announcement marks the 29th Player of the Week selection of his career, including first with the Heat, and the 66th time in the franchise’s 39 season a Heat player has been so cited. He was named NBA Eastern Conference Player of the Week for the period of Nov. 9-17.
 San Antonio Spurs center Victor Wembanyama was named NBA Western Conference Player of the Week.
 Antetokounmpo helped lead Miami to a 3-0 record during the judging period, averaging 33.7 points, 11.3 rebounds, 4.7 assists and 1.33 blocks. He scored at least 30 points in each contest and led the team in all three games in scoring and rebounding, and in blocks twice, posting two double-doubles and missing a third by a single rebound.
